items.title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
items.excerpt: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much it thinks, and record which reading it chooses. A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes.…

items.title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting

Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. items.title: Stream low-latency speech from AI agents using Kokoro TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI
items.excerpt: Voice agents often wait for an agent's full response before starting speech synthesis, adding latency users feel directly. This post shows how to stream each sentence to a Kokoro-82M text-to-speech model on Amazon SageMaker AI as the agent produces it, and how to get that audio back to a browser over Server-Sent Events or a unified binary transport.
